newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends mostly weaker in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends mostly weaker in slow trading.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended mostly lower in subdued range-bound activity as the market waits for the August 12 U.S. Department of Agriculture crop report, traders and analysts said.
Most active December cotton lost 0.28 cent to end at 74.84 cents a lb while the rest of the board was 0.18 up to 0.25 cent weaker.
Floor sources said the trade was a seller above 75.20 cents, basis December and a buyer below 75.00 cents.
"The funds have not been active," one floor source said. About 5,000 lots changed hands in thin volume, traders said.
"The market is waiting for the August crop estimate with objective yield surveys for some states," Merrill Lynch vice president Judith Ganes said.
But she said she does not expect any significant changes until the September production report.
On the fundamental side, analysts cited reports of rain in northern China which suffered from a drought as well as rains in west Texas and the Memphis area.
"Memphis territory had some rain and they need it for their cotton," Prudential Securities analyst Ernest Simon said.
"Usually this time of the year, it is the quietest time for the cotton market," Simon added.
